config.title: Discriminated Union Props

intro.title: Discriminated Union Props
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple Vue component that displays different types of user notifications, such as success messages, warnings, and errors. You'll learn how to use discriminated union props, a TypeScript pattern that ensures your component only receives valid combinations of data based on a shared property (like 'type'). The main technologies involved are Vue 3's Composition API with TypeScript, using defineProps for type-safe props. By the end, you'll understand how to define and use a union of object types to make your components more robust and self-documenting.
intro.usecase: Discriminated union props are essential when building UI components that need to handle multiple distinct states or variants with clear type safety. You'll see this pattern in dashboard cards that display different content types (metrics, charts, alerts), form steps with varying input requirements, or notification systems showing success/error/warning messages. This approach ensures your components handle each variant correctly while providing excellent TypeScript support and preventing runtime errors.

objectives: Construct a Vue component that accepts a discriminated union prop
Configure TypeScript interfaces to define a discriminated union type
Implement conditional rendering based on the discriminator property
Bind component data to different UI structures for each union variant
Manipulate component state to switch between discriminated union cases
Initialize component props with different discriminated union values
Render appropriate content by checking the discriminator property

steps.title: Import Vue and defineProps
steps.instruction: Import Vue and define a component with defineProps. Start by creating a Vue component file with the necessary import and props definition.
steps.hint: In Vue, you need to import the createApp function from 'vue' and use defineProps to declare component props.
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and define a component with defineProps
steps.expectedOutcome: The component file will have the Vue import and a props definition structure ready for discriminated union props.
successCriteria: Vue is imported from 'vue' and the component exports an object with a props property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import Vue and define the props structure correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement and the component structure. You need to import Vue and define props.

steps.title: Create base component structure
steps.instruction: Create the main component structure with a template and script setup section. Use the Vue SFC (Single File Component) format.
steps.hint: In Vue, a component typically has a <template> section for the HTML structure and a <script setup> section for the JavaScript logic.
steps.analogousExample: // Example of a basic Vue component structure
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a basic Vue component structure with template and script setup sections ready for implementing discriminated union props.
successCriteria: The component has both <template> and <script setup> sections in valid Vue SFC format.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the <template> and <script setup> sections. The template should contain a <div> wrapper.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't complete. Remember that Vue components need both template and script sections. Try creating a <template> with a <div> and a <script setup> section.

steps.title: Define discriminated union prop structure
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, use defineProps to define a prop called 'type' that accepts either 'text' or 'number' as string values.
steps.hint: In Vue's Composition API with <script setup>, you can use defineProps to declare component props. For this step, define a prop with a specific set of allowed string values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a prop 'type' that acts as a discriminator, accepting only 'text' or 'number' values.
successCriteria: defineProps is used to declare a prop named 'type' with a validator that checks for 'text' or 'number' values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the validator function correctly checks for both 'text' and 'number' values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The prop definition doesn't match the required structure. Remember to use defineProps with a validator that accepts only 'text' or 'number' values.

steps.title: Add first union type: success message
steps.instruction: Add a 'message' prop to the defineProps object that is required when the 'type' prop equals 'text'.
steps.hint: Inside the defineProps object, add a 'message' property with type: String and required: true. This will be the first variant of your discriminated union.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now accepts a 'message' prop that is required when using the 'text' type variant.
successCriteria: The defineProps object includes a 'message' property with type: String and required: true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the 'message' prop has both 'type: String' and 'required: true' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'message' prop should be added to the defineProps object with type: String and required: true. Try adding it after the 'type' prop.

steps.title: Add second union type: error message
steps.instruction: Add a second prop definition for an error message variant. Include an 'error' prop (String, required) and ensure the 'type' prop validator also accepts 'error' as a valid value.
steps.hint: Add a new property to the defineProps object for the error message, and update the validator array to include 'error'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has props for both success and error message variants, with 'type' accepting 'text', 'number', and 'error' values.
successCriteria: The defineProps object includes an 'error' prop (String, required) and the 'type' validator includes 'error' in its array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some props, but make sure both the 'error' prop and updated 'type' validator are present.
steps.feedbackWrong: The props definition doesn't match the requirements. Check that you added the 'error' prop and updated the 'type' validator.

steps.title: Add third union type: loading state
steps.instruction: Add a third variant to the discriminated union props for a loading state. Extend the defineProps object to include a 'loading' property that is a Boolean, and update the validator to also accept 'loading' as a valid type value.
steps.hint: Add a new property called 'loading' with type: Boolean, and modify the validator array to include 'loading'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The defineProps object now includes a 'loading' property of type Boolean, and the validator for 'type' accepts 'loading' as a valid value.
successCriteria: The props object includes a 'loading' property with type: Boolean, and the validator array includes 'loading'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both the 'loading' property and the updated validator are correctly added.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the 'loading' property with type: Boolean and updated the validator to include 'loading'.

steps.title: Create computed property for type checking
steps.instruction: Inside the script setup section, create a computed property named 'isSuccess' that returns true when the 'type' prop equals 'success'.
steps.hint: Use Vue's computed function to create a reactive property that depends on the type prop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example computed property
const isActive = computed(() => props.status === 'active')
steps.expectedOutcome: A computed property 'isSuccess' is created that checks if the type prop equals 'success'.
successCriteria: The computed property 'isSuccess' is defined and returns true when type equals 'success'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the computed property correctly checks if type equals 'success'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property isn't set up correctly. Remember to use computed() and check the type prop value.

steps.title: Add template structure with conditional rendering
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a div with v-if conditions to render content based on the 'type' prop value. Start with a condition for 'text' type.
steps.hint: Use v-if on a div element to check if type equals 'text'. You'll add more conditions for other types in later steps.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a conditional div that will only render when the 'type' prop equals 'text'.
successCriteria: Template contains a div element with v-if="type === 'text'" condition
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element with the exact v-if condition checking if type equals 'text'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should include a div with v-if="type === 'text'" to conditionally render content based on the discriminator prop.

steps.title: Render success message content
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a new div element that conditionally renders when the type prop equals 'success'. Inside this div, add a paragraph element with the text 'Operation completed successfully!'
steps.hint: Use v-if directive to conditionally render the div based on the type prop value. Remember to use the correct prop name from your defineProps definition.
steps.analogousExample: // Conditional rendering based on a prop
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now display a success message when the type prop is set to 'success', implementing one variant of the discriminated union pattern.
successCriteria: A div element with v-if="type === 'success'" contains a paragraph with the success message text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the conditional div and the paragraph with the exact success message text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The success message content isn't properly implemented. Check that you've added a div with v-if="type === 'success'" containing a paragraph with the message text.

steps.title: Render error and loading content
steps.instruction: Add conditional rendering for the error and loading states in your template. Use v-else-if directives to display appropriate content when the type prop is 'error' or 'loading'.
steps.hint: After your existing v-if for type 'text', add v-else-if branches for 'error' and 'loading'. Inside each, add a div with appropriate content.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional rendering for different states
Success!
Error occurred
Loading...
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will now display different content based on the type prop value, including error and loading states.
successCriteria: Template contains v-else-if branches for 'error' and 'loading' types with appropriate content
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have both v-else-if branches for 'error' and 'loading' with appropriate content.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added v-else-if directives for both 'error' and 'loading' states with appropriate content inside each.
